what_it_does: Cloud servers run many virtual machines (VMs) — software-isolated pretend-computers — on shared physical hardware, and those VMs need fast access to storage drives that use the NVMe protocol (a modern standard for talking to fast solid-state drives). Existing approaches either route every storage command through an extra software layer (slow, burns CPU) or dedicate hardware ports to individual VMs (fast but you can only have a handful of VMs). NVMePass is a combined software and hardware design that lets each VM send commands directly to the storage drive and receive completions back, with no CPU involved in the middle. A new piece of logic inside the drive controller called an NVMe Resource Domain (NRD) acts as a gatekeeper, blocking any VM from accessing storage regions that belong to another VM, so isolation is maintained without the overhead of a middleman.
